content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/code-review

# Code Review

## Overview

**They find, you fix.** Follow the spirit, not the letter: dispatching a
reviewer satisfies the letter; one that read an empty diff, or that you never
waited for, looked at nothing and found nothing. The rule is that
somebody who did not write the change has said what is wrong with it — and that
cannot be you. You read the change you meant to make, not the one on disk.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** A finding you settled in your head is one they meet as a bug,
with nothing saying anyone saw it.

## The Iron Law

```
NO CHANGE IS DONE UNTIL A READ-ONLY REVIEWER HAS SEEN IT AND
EVERY CRITICAL AND IMPORTANT FINDING IS RESOLVED OR RECORDED AS DEFERRED.
```

**Read-only** is a trust boundary, not a performance note: the reviewer reads
anything, runs read-only checks, and writes nothing — not source, not git, not
run state. You stay the single writer.

No exceptions. The first names its addressee; the rest hold for anyone.

- **Never run a reviewer in the background — you, the agent in a herdr pane,
  where ending a turn *is* how you report done.** Do not set
  `run_in_background`, do not yield, and do not schedule a wakeup while one is
  out. A backgrounded reviewer parks you mid-turn, indistinguishable from a
  finished turn, and the run stalls until a human nudges the pane. Dispatch it
  blocking and read its verdict in the turn you dispatched it. That reason is
  role-specific, so there is exactly one role it does not bind: a **driver**
  reviewing its own inline change, which may background the panel and end the
  turn because its harness re-invokes it on process exit. Inside a pipeline
  run the driver has no panel to background — the task agent's is the gate,
  and `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md` says so at its own loop. In a pane, the
  prohibition is yours.
- **Do not judge a change too small to review.** A one-line edit to a condition
  is the size this skill exists for. Dispatch a reviewer over it.
- **Do not count your own read as the review.** Re-reading your diff tells you
  it matches what you intended — the one thing never in doubt. Dispatch someone
  who does not know it.
- **Do not leave it for the pipeline's review phase.** That phase reads what you
  hand it, after later work is built on it. Dispatch here, while the change is
  one commit wide.
- **Do not close a finding by disagreeing with it.** When you will not fix one,
  quote it and write the reason in the report or handoff. An unrecorded
  decision reads downstream like an unread finding.
- **Do not repeat a verdict you have not read.** Open the file the reviewer
  names, or re-run the review when it named none. A reviewer that never came
  back has not said "clean".

## Announce

Say this out loud before dispatching anything:

```
Using drovr:code-review — dispatching read-only reviewers before calling this done.
```

## The procedure

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

Re-create those items for each change you review, not once for the session.

1. **Write down the change and the exact range** — the files, and `<base>..HEAD`.
   Get it wrong and the reviewer reports clean on nothing.
2. **Dispatch read-only reviewers, blocking, one per angle:** run
   `drovr code-review run <run> <task>` (`<base>` from `<task>-base.sha`, recorded
   before your first edit) — or, **inline** with no run,
   `drovr code-review run --base "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" <task>`. Nothing
   else, and never invent a run to get one.

   It spawns one reviewer per **configured** angle — `config.angles`, which
   defaults to correctness, security, error-handling, type-design — each writing
   `<task>-review-<angle>.json`, merged into `<task>-review.json`. **Read the
   config, not this page**, and cover any lens it omits yourself.

   Tell each reviewer to review as a skeptic, not the author; to say whether the
   tests exercise the behaviour, not just that they pass; to rate every finding
   **Critical, Important or nit** — what the Iron Law gates on — and say so when
   it found none; and to write them to a path you name, so step 3 has something
   to open. The lenses to cover:
   - **Spec compliance** — what was agreed, no more, no less?
   - **Correctness** — real bugs, unhandled cases, broken invariants.
   - **Verification** — do the claimed tests exist, and would they fail on a
     regression?
   - **Quality** — reuse, simplification, consistency with the code around it.
3. **Wait for every reviewer, then read what each wrote.** Open the findings
   file by path, then classify the round by how the panel exited:

   | Exit | What it means |
   |---|---|
   | 0 | clean — a real range was reviewed, nothing blocking |
   | 3 | blocking findings; go to step 5 |
   | 2 | timeout — reviewers are slow, not broken. Re-run the same command: it resumes the panel in flight |
   | 1 | error, or an empty `<base>..HEAD` it refused. Fix the range or the setup; never re-run blindly |
   | 137/143 | **your own harness killed it.** drovr produced no verdict at all, and none of the rows above describes the run. Re-run to resume, and record the round as **unclassifiable** — never as a timeout |

   A reviewer that returned no verdict is none of the five: re-dispatch rather
   than report its silence.

   **Only 0 is clean, and one clean round does not end the loop.** Stop at
   whichever of two comes first — **there is no round cap**, and a loop still
   turning up Critical or Important findings is not finished at any count:
   - **Two consecutive clean rounds over an unchanged HEAD.** Any edit between
     them resets the count — the second round is evidence about the first only
     if it read the same code.
   - **Two consecutive rounds that lost a dimension** — its own outcome, *not*
     a clean ending: a missing angle is a Critical stand-in, so a round that
     lost a reviewer never measured the code, and a panel that keeps failing to
     deliver is not going to. Name the angles that never ran, write up every
     round's verdict and everything still open (step 5), and finish on that
     record rather than on a verdict. Without this a panel whose reviewers keep
     dying cannot end at all, since such a round is never clean.

   Two caveats the rule owes you. Two cleans make a false clean **less
   likely**, not unlikely, and prove nothing about convergence — in forge#88's
   own data two consecutive cleans preceded a `changes` round with seven
   findings. And every word of this is prose nothing enforces — the
   shape of the *"re-run it"* that produced 47 re-arms over 14 hours.
4. **Check what the reviewer actually read — range *and* working tree.** The
   range must be the whole of `<base>..HEAD`, every file you touched, not a
   subset you picked; **and uncommitted work is in scope, not exempt** — drovr's
   panel reviews the diff *plus the current working tree*. A verdict covers what
   is on disk only if the reviewer saw both. Clean on an empty range, a subset,
   or a tree with unreviewed edits in it is about a change nobody read.
5. **Resolve every Critical and Important finding, or record the deferral with
   `drovr code-review defer`.** Per finding: quote it, then name the edit
   answering it by file — or, if you are not making it, run

   ```
   drovr code-review defer <RUN> <TASK> --file <path> [--line <n>] \
     --severity <critical|important|nit> --summary "<the finding>" \
     --reason "<why it is not being fixed>"
   ```

   A deferral written only in prose is one the next round cannot read, so it
   re-raises the finding you already ruled on. The command appends to a
   per-task log every later seed carries; prose does not.
6. **Re-run the checks after your last review-driven edit, then say it is
   done.** The fixes are new, unverified code: run the tests. When the change is
   not code and has no suite, name what you re-read instead and why it covers the
   edits — written down, never assumed. Report the findings, the edits and the
   deferrals; inside a drovr phase this also gates `drovr phase done`. **Done is
   step 3's termination rule met, not the first exit 0** — say which of the
   two ended it, and on a lost dimension say plainly that the loop ended on a
   record rather than on a clean verdict.

## Requirements

The middle column is what the claim takes; the right is what gets accepted
instead.

| The claim | Required evidence | NOT sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| *"This change has been reviewed"* | A read-only reviewer dispatched over this change in the foreground, returned in this turn, and the range you handed it, written down | Your own re-read · a reviewer launched and not waited for · a review of the tree before your last edit |
| *"The reviewer found nothing"* | The findings file it wrote, opened by path and read by you — or the review re-run by you when it wrote none — **and** what it read shown to be the whole of `<base>..HEAD` **plus your working tree** | Its summary, however much output it pastes · exit 1 or 2 · a subset of your files · uncommitted edits nobody looked at · a verdict that never arrived |
| *"Every Critical and Important finding is resolved"* | Each quoted, the edit answering it named by file, and step 6's checks re-run after the last edit | A count · agreeing with one in prose · fixing the Criticals and leaving the Importants |
| *"That finding does not apply here"* | The finding quoted, and the reason written where the next agent reads it | Deciding it in your head · *"out of scope"* with no scope named · silence, which downstream reads as resolved |

## Red flags — STOP

Some are thoughts, some are things you have just written. Either way you are at
the line.

- *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* · *"The lead said just
  send it."* · *"It is a two-line change."* · *"I already reviewed it myself."*
  · *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* — each opens a row in
  *Rationalizations*, verbatim. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are about to launch a reviewer in the background and keep working.* →
  Dispatch it blocking. No version of that ends with you reading its verdict
  this turn.
- *A reviewer has not come back and you are writing the report.* → Block on it.
  Silence is not a pass; a parked reviewer is not a finished one.
- *The panel came back clean in seconds on a large diff.* → Check what it read.
  Clean and empty look identical from here.
- **Anything that treats the change as finished** — any wording at all, and
  also committing, opening a PR, or starting the next task — while a reviewer is
  unread, unreturned, or holding an unresolved Critical or Important finding. If
  you cannot name the reviewer and point at what it wrote, change what you
  dispatched, not how you word it.

## Rationalizations

The right column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* | Dispatch the reviewer first, then send it. Two different reads: theirs is for fit, the review's is for correctness, and one does not make the other redundant — reading a document aloud catches prose gaps, not retry semantics. |
| *"The lead said just send it."* | Send it after the review, and tell them the call moves. That is a scheduling reflex, not anyone weighing the technical risk — the calendar is theirs, the correctness yours. |
| *"It is a two-line change."* | Dispatch a reviewer over the two lines. Size is not a risk measure, and the risk you estimate in order to skip the review is what it would have told you. |
| *"I already reviewed it myself."* | Dispatch one that did not write it. Your read confirms the diff matches your intent; the defects worth catching are in what you did not think of. |
| *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* | Dispatch here, now. That phase reads what you hand it, after later tasks built on it; a finding costs more at every step it survives. |
| *"The reviewer came back with no findings."* | Open the file it named, and check it read your whole change, working tree included. An empty range comes back clean from every angle at once. |

## Worked example

One read away, in `skills/code-review/worked-example.md`: a 320-line spec, a
client call in 19 minutes, a $45,000 sign-off and a lead writing *"just send
it"* — the rationalization refused, the panel run, two Importants found, the
call moved 22 minutes. Worth reading once; the rules above do not depend on it.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you repeat a
  verdict: a reviewer's report is a claim, not evidence.
- `drovr:systematic-debugging` — REQUIRED when a finding is a bug: it is a
  report, not a diagnosis. Reproduce before you fix.
- `drovr:tdd` — REQUIRED when a finding needs new behaviour: the fix is new code
  and gets a failing test.
- `drovr:handoff` — REQUIRED at a phase boundary: deferred findings travel in the
  handoff or not at all.
- `drovr:pipeline` — whose gate this is in a run: yours, the task agent's, run
  to step 3's termination rule before `drovr phase done`. The driver reads your
  record of it and runs no panel of its own.

   panel reviews the diff *plus the current working tree*. A verdict covers what
   is on disk only if the reviewer saw both. Clean on an empty range, a subset,
   or a tree with unreviewed edits in it is about a change nobody read.
5. **Resolve every Critical and Important finding, or record the deferral with
   `drovr code-review defer`.** Per finding: quote it, then name the edit
   answering it by file — or, if you are not making it, run

   ```
   drovr code-review defer <RUN> <TASK> --file <path> [--line <n>] \
     --severity <critical|important|nit> --summary "<the finding>" \
     --reason "<why it is not being fixed>"
   ```

   A deferral written only in prose is one the next round cannot read, so it
   re-raises the finding you already ruled on. The command appends to a
   per-task log every later seed carries; prose does not.
6. **Re-run the checks after your last review-driven edit, then say it is
   done.** The fixes are new, unverified code: run the tests. When the change is
   not code and has no suite, name what you re-read instead and why it covers the
   edits — written down, never assumed. Report the findings, the edits and the
   deferrals; inside a drovr phase this also gates `drovr phase done`. **Done is
   step 3's termination rule met, not the first exit 0** — say which of the
   two ended it, and on a lost dimension say plainly that the loop ended on a
   record rather than on a clean verdict.

## Requirements

The middle column is what the claim takes; the right is what gets accepted
instead.

| The claim | Required evidence | NOT sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| *"This change has been reviewed"* | A read-only reviewer dispatched over this change in the foreground, returned in this turn, and the range you handed it, written down | Your own re-read · a reviewer launched and not waited for · a review of the tree before your last edit |
| *"The reviewer found nothing"* | The findings file it wrote, opened by path and read by you — or the review re-run by you when it wrote none — **and** what it read shown to be the whole of `<base>..HEAD` **plus your working tree** | Its summary, however much output it pastes · exit 1 or 2 · a subset of your files · uncommitted edits nobody looked at · a verdict that never arrived |
| *"Every Critical and Important finding is resolved"* | Each quoted, the edit answering it named by file, and step 6's checks re-run after the last edit | A count · agreeing with one in prose · fixing the Criticals and leaving the Importants |
| *"That finding does not apply here"* | The finding quoted, and the reason written where the next agent reads it | Deciding it in your head · *"out of scope"* with no scope named · silence, which downstream reads as resolved |

## Red flags — STOP

Some are thoughts, some are things you have just written. Either way you are at
the line.

- *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* · *"The lead said just
  send it."* · *"It is a two-line change."* · *"I already reviewed it myself."*
  · *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* — each opens a row in
  *Rationalizations*, verbatim. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are about to launch a reviewer in the background and keep working.* →
  Dispatch it blocking. No version of that ends with you reading its verdict
  this turn.
- *A reviewer has not come back and you are writing the report.* → Block on it.
  Silence is not a pass; a parked reviewer is not a finished one.
- *The panel came back clean in seconds on a large diff.* → Check what it read.
  Clean and empty look identical from here.
- **Anything that treats the change as finished** — any wording at all, and
  also committing, opening a PR, or starting the next task — while a reviewer is
  unread, unreturned, or holding an unresolved Critical or Important finding. If
  you cannot name the reviewer and point at what it wrote, change what you
  dispatched, not how you word it.

## Rationalizations

The right column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* | Dispatch the reviewer first, then send it. Two different reads: theirs is for fit, the review's is for correctness, and one does not make the other redundant — reading a document aloud catches prose gaps, not retry semantics. |
| *"The lead said just send it."* | Send it after the review, and tell them the call moves. That is a scheduling reflex, not anyone weighing the technical risk — the calendar is theirs, the correctness yours. |
| *"It is a two-line change."* | Dispatch a reviewer over the two lines. Size is not a risk measure, and the risk you estimate in order to skip the review is what it would have told you. |
| *"I already reviewed it myself."* | Dispatch one that did not write it. Your read confirms the diff matches your intent; the defects worth catching are in what you did not think of. |
| *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* | Dispatch here, now. That phase reads what you hand it, after later tasks built on it; a finding costs more at every step it survives. |
| *"The reviewer came back with no findings."* | Open the file it named, and check it read your whole change, working tree included. An empty range comes back clean from every angle at once. |

## Worked example

One read away, in `skills/code-review/worked-example.md`: a 320-line spec, a
client call in 19 minutes, a $45,000 sign-off and a lead writing *"just send
it"* — the rationalization refused, the panel run, two Importants found, the
call moved 22 minutes. Worth reading once; the rules above do not depend on it.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you repeat a
  verdict: a reviewer's report is a claim, not evidence.
- `drovr:systematic-debugging` — REQUIRED when a finding is a bug: it is a
  report, not a diagnosis. Reproduce before you fix.
- `drovr:tdd` — REQUIRED when a finding needs new behaviour: the fix is new code
  and gets a failing test.
- `drovr:handoff` — REQUIRED at a phase boundary: deferred findings travel in the
  handoff or not at all.
- `drovr:pipeline` — whose gate this is in a run: yours, the task agent's, run
  to step 3's termination rule before `drovr phase done`. The driver reads your
  record of it and runs no panel of its own.

1:#!/usr/bin/env bash
2:# Cases for the claim that orca.nix runs the Orca GUI unsandboxed: the
3:# AppImage's tree patched with autoPatchelf and wrapped with makeWrapper, not
4:# appimageTools' bwrap FHS env.
5:#
6:# Why this needs a test. Inside the FHS env, everything Orca spawns -- its
7:# terminals and the agents in them -- saw the env's /usr, not the host's:
8:# /etc/hostname was missing, `date` printed UTC (/etc/localtime points into
9:# /usr/share/zoneinfo), every font fell to Montserrat Thin. And bwrap stood
10:# between every caller and Electron, forwarding no signals. None of that shows
11:# from the host, only from a process the app spawns, so these cases probe from
12:# one.
13:#
14:# The probes run on the host. When this script itself runs inside a sandbox
15:# (an Orca terminal on the old build has no /etc/hostname), each probe goes
16:# through `systemd-run --user`, whose units the user manager starts outside it.
17:#
18:# Two trees are deliberately left unpatched and must stay byte-identical:
19:# resources/node-runtime, whose node is copied into orcad slots and checked
20:# against a sha256 pin in app.asar (a patched node fails the check, and Orca
21:# falls back to downloading stock node), and resources/orcad-template, whose
22:# per-target builds (arm64, musl) are shipped to remote hosts.
23:#
24:# The GUI case (6) opens a real, visible window on the desktop, so it runs
25:# only with ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 -- ask before setting it on someone's session.
26:# It starts a second instance with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway
27:# HOME, so it never touches the running Orca's profile, its
28:# ~/.orca/agent-hooks or ~/.claude/settings.json.
29:#
30:#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
31:#   ORCA_TEST_GUI=1 tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh   ... and launch it once
32:#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh <orca-path>   test a given build, e.g. the live one:
33:#                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
34:set -u
35:set -o pipefail
36:
37:fails=0; n=0
38:pass() { n=$((n+1)); echo "ok   $1"; }
39:fail() { n=$((n+1)); echo "FAIL $1: $2"; fails=$((fails+1)); }
40:
41:FLAKE=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
42:
43:if [ -e /etc/hostname ]; then
44:  host() { "$@"; }
45:else
46:  sr=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" 'nixpkgs#systemd^out') \
47:    || { echo "inside a sandbox and could not build systemd-run" >&2; exit 1; }
48:  # Through /bin/sh, so the command is looked up on the host's PATH, not here.
49:  host() { "$sr/bin/systemd-run" --user --pipe --wait --quiet /bin/sh -c 'exec "$@"' sh "$@"; }
50:fi
51:HOSTNAME_=$(host cat /etc/hostname) || { echo "cannot reach the host" >&2; exit 1; }
52:
53:ORCA="${1:-}"
54:if [ -z "$ORCA" ]; then
55:  drv=$(nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$HOSTNAME_.config.home.packages" \
56:    --apply 'ps: (builtins.head (builtins.filter (p: builtins.match "orca-[0-9.]+" (p.name or "") != null) ps)).drvPath') \
57:    || { echo "orca is not in home.packages here" >&2; exit 1; }
58:  ORCA=$(nix-store --realise "$drv" | tail -1) || { echo "could not build orca" >&2; exit 1; }
59:fi
60:ORCA=$(readlink -f "$ORCA")
61:
62:# The desktop file's Exec names the GUI bin, whatever it is called this week.
63:exe=$(sed -n 's/^Exec=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$ORCA"/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop | head -1)
64:GUI="$ORCA/bin/$exe"
65:[ -n "$exe" ] && [ -x "$GUI" ] || { echo "no GUI bin from $ORCA's desktop Exec ('$exe')" >&2; exit 1; }
66:echo "testing $GUI"
67:
68:T=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.cache/orca-gui-test.XXXXXX"); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
69:
70:# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
71:if nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | grep -q -- '-bubblewrap-'; then
72:  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"
73:else
74:  pass "no bubblewrap in the closure"
75:fi
150:got=$(sha256sum "$node" 2>/dev/null | cut -d' ' -f1)
151:[ -n "$pin" ] && [ "$got" = "$pin" ] && pass "bundled node matches orcad's runtime pin" \
152:  || fail "node pin" "sha256 '$got', pin '${pin:-missing}'"
153:
154:# 6. A real second instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and stops on
155:# SIGTERM. Its own --user-data-dir and HOME keep it off the live Orca's state.
156:if [ "${ORCA_TEST_GUI:-}" != 1 ]; then
157:  echo "skip GUI launch: it opens a visible window; set ORCA_TEST_GUI=1"
158:elif [ -z "$(host printenv WAYLAND_DISPLAY)" ]; then
159:  echo "skip GUI launch: no Wayland session"
160:else

I reviewed commit f888db7d (`39c256fd..HEAD`). `git status` was clean when I started. Partway through, `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh` was changed in the working tree (not committed): case 6 now runs in a headless sway. I reviewed the committed version and only mention the change where it matters.

**What checks out:**
- **Pinned trees:** `resources/node-runtime` and `resources/orcad-template` match the AppImage byte for byte (`diff -r --no-dereference`). File modes are kept (node is still 555) and node's sha256 matches `.runtime-node`.
- **Wrapper:** every step from the home-manager wrapper through nixGL to makeWrapper uses `exec`, so the process you launch is Electron itself. `"$@"` comes through intact (tested with `'a b' '' '$x'`). In node mode `FONTCONFIG_FILE` is set and no ozone flag is added.
- **Desktop file:** `Exec=orca-ide %U`, `x-scheme-handler/orca` is still there, and the icons are installed at 16 to 512.

## Important

1. **The Wayland clipboard helper can't find its library** (orca.nix:55-58). `resources/bin/orca-wayland-clipboard` loads `libwayland-client.so.0` at runtime. After patching, its search path covers only libglvnd, systemd, libsecret, libnotify and libappindicator, plus nix glibc's own directory.
   - My shell turned out to be inside the old bwrap environment, where a fake `/etc/ld.so.cache` and `/lib` hid the failure. The real store path has no cache file, so on the Arch host this load should fail. The unpatched AppImage binary found the host's library. I could not run it on the host itself.
   - Fix: add `pkgs.wayland` to `runtimeDependencies`.
2. **Chromium's audio and video libraries are missing** (same lines). `orca-ide` loads `libpulse.so.0`, `libpipewire-0.3.so.0` and `libva` at runtime, and none of them is reachable now. The old bwrap environment supplied all three.
   - Orca has dictation (`stt-worker`, the sherpa-onnx speech addons) and plays sounds. Without PulseAudio, Chromium falls back to nix's ALSA, which can't use the host's PipeWire/Pulse plugin, so mic and sound likely fail. Screen capture through the portal goes too.
   - Fix: add `libpulseaudio pipewire libva` to `runtimeDependencies`.
3. **nixGL's environment now leaks into host programs** (orca.nix:244). nixGL exports `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` (nix mesa and libglvnd) and several driver variables, and every process Orca spawns inherits them. Inside bwrap that did no harm; now the terminals run host binaries.
   - A host GL program started from an Orca terminal (mpv, chromium, another Electron app) would load nix mesa next to its own libraries. Expect `GLIBCXX` version errors, crashes or the wrong driver. This is inferred; I didn't run it on the host.
4. **Test case 4 (ldd) checks with the wrong loader** (test:126). `ldd` uses its own loader, not the one the binary names (confirmed in `/usr/bin/ldd` at lines 29 and 176). On Arch that loader searches `/etc/ld.so.cache` and `/usr/lib`, so a library dropped from the search path still reports as found if Arch has it installed. It also can't see runtime-loaded libraries, which is why items 1 and 2 pass.
   - Fix: run each file's own interpreter (`LD_TRACE_LOADED_OBJECTS=1 "$interp" f`) and add explicit checks for the runtime-loaded libraries.
5. **Losing `--ozone-platform=wayland` passes the default run** (test:156). Only case 6 starts the app in GUI mode, and it needs `ORCA_TEST_GUI=1`. Case 2 only checks that node mode doesn't get the flag. The uncommitted headless-sway version of case 6 would catch this once committed.

## Nits

- **N1** (orca.nix:60-63). The comment saying the fixup steps run "by hand, or not at all" around the pinned trees is wrong. Shebang patching and rpath shrinking still run over them. They change nothing today only because the two scripts with shebangs (`orcad-template/out/cli/index.js`, `runtime.py`) aren't executable. Test 5 would catch a change.
- **N2** (orca.nix:40-43). AppRun added `--no-sandbox` when user namespaces were unavailable. That fallback is gone, so on such a host Chromium aborts on the non-setuid `chrome-sandbox`. Fine on this Arch host.
- **N3.** There is no `wrapGAppsHook3`, so GSettings schemas and GIO modules come from the host's `/usr/share`. The GTK file chooser fallback works only if the host has gtk3's schemas. Desktop launches also get no `LOCALE_ARCHIVE` for nix glibc.
- **N4** (test:71). `nix-store -qR | grep -q` under `pipefail` can report "no bubblewrap" when bubblewrap is present: `grep -q` exits early, nix-store gets SIGPIPE and the `else` branch passes. It doesn't happen today only because the 14 KB listing fits in the pipe buffer.
- **N5** (test:84). Only `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1` is tested, not empty or `0`.
- **N6** (test:94). `date +%Z` passes on a UTC host whatever the build does. The `readlink /etc/localtime` check covers it.
- **N7** (test:102-110). The font cases run the host's `fc-list`/`fc-match`, not Electron's own built-in fontconfig. They do still fail if `FONTCONFIG_FILE` is dropped.
- **N8** (test:113-117). In the node-pty case, output can arrive after the exit event and print `" 0"`. That is a flaky false failure, not a false pass.
- **N9** (test:120-125). If `file` isn't on the host, the message says "only 0 ELFs found", which is misleading. It still fails.
- **N10** (test:140). `diff -r` ignores file modes, so a lost exec bit on node would pass case 5. The modes are correct today.
- **N11** (test:68, 161-199). If `mktemp` fails, `"$T/home"` becomes `/home`. The exit trap doesn't stop the test's systemd unit, so an interrupted run leaves a second Orca running on a profile being deleted.
- **N12** (test:78). Finding the app directory depends on `nix-store -qR` listing the inner package before the nixGL wrapper, which also contains `lib/orca`. It works today.

content.text:
Round 1 is fixed and committed (3b9add58). The test passes 17/17, and its GUI case now runs only in a private headless sway, so nothing appears on your desktop. Round 2 is running on the new HEAD.

Real bugs round 1 found and fixed:
- **Wayland clipboard helper was broken.** It couldn't find `libwayland-client`/`libgtk-3`, and its `--probe` exited 69. It now passes.
- **Electron couldn't load its audio and video libraries:** PulseAudio, PipeWire (used for screen capture) and libva. They're now added.
- **`strip` was rewriting the pinned node and the orcad-template files.** I caught this myself before review. <result>I found no Critical issues, six Important ones and several nits. The two most serious: a third set of hash-pinned files that the build can change without failing, and the "headless" GUI test still talks to your real desktop session bus.

The worktree is clean and HEAD is 3b9add58. The test against the wrapper passed 17/17. The build log confirms installCheckPhase runs after fixup and checks the final tree (it printed `node: OK` and `diff -r` was silent). It would fail the build on any diff, sha mismatch or an AppRun left in place.

These already work as intended:
- autoPatchelf skips the two pinned directories.
- The extra runtime libraries do land on the executables' library path.
- The wayland flag goes first, so Orca's own `serve --ozone-platform=x11` still wins.
- An empty `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` is treated the same way Electron treats it.
- The desktop file reads `Exec=orca-ide %U`, with no `--no-sandbox`, and keeps `x-scheme-handler/orca`.
- All eight icon sizes are there, and every wrapper in the chain uses `exec`.

## Critical
None.

## Important
1. **A third pinned set, `resources/ripgrep`, is neither excluded nor checked** (orca.nix:92-98, 122-130). `orcad-template.json` pins `ripgrep/linux-x64/rg` and `linux-arm64/rg` by sha256 with `"packagedRipgrep": true`. Orca's own code says deployed slots take rg from `resources/` and verify it. Both files are static today, so autoPatchelf skipped them and their hashes match.
   - Failure: a version bump ships a dynamically linked rg. autoPatchelf rewrites its loader to a /nix/store path and the build still passes, while orcad slot installs fail verification or remote hosts get a broken rg.
   - Fix: exclude `*/resources/ripgrep`, and have installCheckPhase check every sha256 listed in `orcad-template.json`.
2. **The headless GUI case shares your real session D-Bus** (test:178-181). The user manager exports `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=unix:path=/run/user/1000/bus`. That is an absolute path, so the private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` doesn't cut it off. It also passes on `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`.
   - Failure: the app uses libsecret (`org.freedesktop.secrets`), so each fresh-profile run can write a key into your real keyring. If the keyring is locked, an unlock prompt appears on your real desktop. Notifications or a tray icon would also reach your real desktop.
   - Fix: run sway under `dbus-run-session` or a private bus, and clear `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE`.
3. **GPU loading depends on nixGL's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, and the dlopen check looks at the wrong file** (orca.nix:58-61; test:157-163). python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='orca.nix'
s=open(p).read()
def rep(old,new):
    global s
    assert old in s, old[:60]
    s=s.replace(old,new)
rep('''  # Two trees stay byte-identical. resources/node-runtime's node is copied
  # into orcad slots and checked against a sha256 pin (the template's
  # targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node); patched -- or stripped -- it
  # fails the check and Orca downloads stock node instead. resources/
  # orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca ships to
  # remote hosts. Both run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader, which
  # Arch is.''','''  # Three trees stay byte-identical: what orcad slots are built from, each
  # file sha256-pinned in resources/orcad-template/orcad-template.json and
  # checked when a slot is installed -- patched or stripped, the check fails
  # and Orca downloads stock copies instead. resources/node-runtime's node is
  # the slot's runtime (pinned by the template's .runtime-node);
  # resources/orcad-template holds per-target builds (arm64, musl) that Orca
  # ships to remote hosts; resources/ripgrep is the slots' rg
  # (packagedRipgrep). All run unpatched on a glibc host with an FHS loader,
  # which Arch is.''')
rep('''          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template) ;;''','''          */resources|*/resources/node-runtime|*/resources/orcad-template|*/resources/ripgrep) ;;''')
rep('''      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
''','''      autoPatchelf -- "''${targets[@]}"
      # runtimeDependencies only reach executables, but Chromium's bundled GL
      # (ANGLE, SwiftShader) dlopens libEGL/libGL itself, and a dlopen
      # searches the calling library's RUNPATH. Without this they find GL
      # only through nixGL's LD_LIBRARY_PATH -- as nixpkgs' electron-bin does.
      patchelf --add-rpath ${lib.makeLibraryPath orcaRuntimeDeps} \\

# dlopened, so autoPatchelf cannot see them, and nix's loader has no
    # /usr/lib to fall back on: GL and udev for the GPU process, pulse and
    # pipewire for audio and screen capture, libva for video decode,
    # libsecret for Electron's safeStorage, notify and appindicator for
    # notifications and the tray; wayland-client and gtk3 for
    # resources/bin/orca-wayland-clipboard, which links only libc.
    runtimeDependencies = map lib.getLib orcaRuntimeDeps;
    # The pinned trees, checked where it gates the build: byte for byte the
    # AppImage's (fixup's strip and patchShebangs run over them too; today
    # patchShebangs finds no node or python on PATH, and leaves them alone),
    # and the node still the one orcad's runtime pin names. No chrome-sandbox
    # escape hatch either: AppRun gone, see installPhase.
    doInstallCheck = true;
    installCheckPhase = ''
      runHook preInstallCheck
      for d in node-runtime orcad-template; do
        diff -r $src/resources/$d $out/lib/orca/resources/$d
      done
      pin=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < $out/lib/orca/resources/orcad-template/targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node)
      echo "$pin  $out/lib/orca/resources/node-runtime/bin/node" | sha256sum -c
      [ ! -e $out/lib/orca/AppRun ]
      runHook postInstallCheck
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  };

p='orca.nix'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index('    # The pinned trees, checked where it gates the build')
b=s.index('    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";\n  };')
s=s[:a]+r"""    # Checked where it gates the build. The pinned trees: byte for byte and
    # mode for mode the AppImage's (fixup's patchShebangs and patchELF still
    # walk them; today they change nothing), and every pin in orcad's
    # manifest holding -- ripgrep/* there is resources/ripgrep
    # (packagedRipgrep). And no way to an unsandboxed Chromium: AppRun gone
    # (see installPhase), and the desktop Exec exactly the wrapper, no
    # --no-sandbox carried over from upstream's line.
    doInstallCheck = true;
    nativeInstallCheckInputs = [ pkgs.jq ];
    installCheckPhase = ''
      runHook preInstallCheck
      res=$out/lib/orca/resources
      for d in node-runtime orcad-template ripgrep; do
        diff -r --no-dereference $src/resources/$d $res/$d
        diff <(cd $src/resources/$d && find . -printf '%m %y %p\n' | sort) \
             <(cd $res/$d && find . -printf '%m %y %p\n' | sort)
      done
      t=$res/orcad-template
      jq -r '(.commonSha256 | to_entries[] | "\(.value)  \(.key)"),
             (.targets | to_entries[] | .key as $t | .value.files | to_entries[]
               | "\(.value)  targets/\($t)/\(.key)")' $t/orcad-template.json \
        | while read -r sha p; do
            f=$t/$p
            case $p in targets/*/ripgrep/*) [ -e "$f" ] || f=$res/''${p#targets/*/} ;; esac
            echo "$sha  $f"
          done | sha256sum -c --quiet
      pin=$(tr -d '[:space:]' < $t/targets/linux-x64-glibc/.runtime-node)
      echo "$pin  $res/node-runtime/bin/node" | sha256sum -c
      [ ! -e $out/lib/orca/AppRun ]
      [ "$(grep '^Exec=' $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop)" = 'Exec=orca-ide %U' ]
      runHook postInstallCheck
    '';
"""+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF

60:# The desktop file's Exec names the GUI bin, whatever it is called this week.
61:exe=$(sed -n 's/^Exec=\([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "$ORCA"/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop | head -1)
62:GUI="$ORCA/bin/$exe"
63:[ -n "$exe" ] && [ -x "$GUI" ] || { echo "no GUI bin from $ORCA's desktop Exec ('$exe')" >&2; exit 1; }
64:echo "testing $GUI"
65:
66:# Under ~/.cache, not /tmp: the bwrap-era sandbox has its own /tmp, which the
67:# host-side probes would not see.
68:unit="orca-gui-test-$$"
69:T=$(mktemp -d "$HOME/.cache/orca-gui-test.XXXXXX") || { echo "mktemp failed" >&2; exit 1; }
70:trap 'host systemctl --user stop "$unit" 2>/dev/null; rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
71:
72:# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
86:# 2. Node mode: the wrapper must not inject --ozone-platform, which node
87:# rejects ("bad option", exit 9). orca's CLI probes the GUI this way.
88:got=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -p 1 2>&1)
89:[ "$got" = 1 ] && pass "ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 runs node" \
90:  || fail "node mode" "printed '$got', want 1"
91:
92:# 3. What a spawned process sees is the host: hostname, zone, fonts.
93:node_run() { # node_run <shell command>: run it from a child of the GUI in node mode
94:  host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \
95:    'process.stdout.write(require("child_process").execFileSync("/bin/sh", ["-c", process.argv[1]]))' \
96:    "$1" 2>&1
97:}
98:for c in 'cat /etc/hostname' 'date +%Z' 'readlink /etc/localtime'; do
99:  want=$(host /bin/sh -c "$c"); got=$(node_run "$c")
100:  [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "child sees host's '$c' ($want)" \
160:         libsecret-1.so.0 libnotify.so.4 libGL.so.1 libEGL.so.1 libudev.so.1
161:       dlopens "$APP/resources/bin/orca-wayland-clipboard" libwayland-client.so.0 libgtk-3.so.0)
162:[ -z "$lost" ] && pass "everything they dlopen is on their RUNPATH" \
163:  || fail "dlopen" "$(printf '\n%s' "$lost")"
164:
165:# 5. A real instance renders, sandboxes its renderers, and exits 0 on
166:# SIGTERM -- in a headless sway of its own, so it needs no desktop and never
167:# appears on one.
168:tools=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths --inputs-from "$FLAKE" nixpkgs#sway nixpkgs#grim) \
169:  || { echo "could not build sway/grim" >&2; exit 1; }
170:sway=$(echo "$tools" | grep -- '-sway-'); grim=$(echo "$tools" | grep -- '-grim-')
171:run="$T/run"; mkdir -p -m700 "$run"; mkdir -p "$T/home"
172:cat > "$T/sway.conf" <<EOF
173:output HEADLESS-1 resolution 1280x800
174:exec /bin/sh -c '"$GUI" --user-data-dir="$T/profile"; echo \$? > "$T/orca.exit"'
175:EOF
176:in_session() { host env -u DISPLAY XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run" WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1 "$@"; }
177:since=$(date +%s)
178:"${sr:+$sr/bin/}systemd-run" --user --quiet --unit="$unit" --setenv=HOME="$T/home" \
179:  --setenv=XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$run" --setenv=WLR_BACKENDS=headless --setenv=WLR_RENDERER=pixman \
180:  --setenv=WLR_LIBINPUT_NO_DEVICES=1 --setenv=WAYLAND_DISPLAY= --setenv=DISPLAY= \
181:  "$sway/bin/sway" -c "$T/sway.conf"
182:pid=""
183:for _ in $(seq 60); do
184:  sleep 1

## Critical
None.

## Important

**I1. `FONTCONFIG_FILE` leaks into every process Orca spawns, which are now host processes** (`/home/sauyon/orca/workspaces/dotfiles/orca-gui-unsandbox/orca.nix`, the `makeWrapper … --set FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}` line in postFixup; test lines 107-118).
- `fontsConf` includes only nixpkgs' `conf.d` (which pulls in `~/.config/fontconfig`) plus DejaVu. It has no `<dir>/usr/share/fonts`; I confirmed that by grepping the generated conf and its `conf.d`.
- Before, children ran inside the FHS environment. Now they are real host processes. Any Arch-built program started from an Orca terminal (an `/usr/bin` GUI app, `fc-match`, Emacs) reads Orca's private fonts.conf and cannot see fonts installed with pacman.
- Example: launch a pacman-installed viewer from an Orca terminal and text that relies on a pacman-only font falls back to a different font or to tofu.
- The test asserts this leak. Case 3's heading says "What a spawned process sees is the host: … fonts", but the font checks prove the child sees `fontsConf`, which is not the host's. That contradicts the stated goal ("orca's children see the host").
- This is the same kind of problem as deferral (a), but it is a different variable and not covered by it. You may decide to fold it into (a).
- Possible fixes: give Electron the variable without passing it to children, or add `/usr/share/fonts` to `fontsConf`. At minimum, fix the test's wording.
- Tests on regression: no. The test enforces the leak.

## nit

- **N1. The headless GUI case is only partly cut off from the real home** (test lines 187-191). The unit gets the user manager's environment, and `~/.config/environment.d/10-home-manager.conf` sets several variables to absolute paths in the real home: `GNUPGHOME=/home/sauyon/.gnupg`, `CARGO_HOME`, `RUSTUP_HOME`, `GOPATH`, `GC_HOME=~/.local/state/gc`, `CODER_SSH_CONFIG_FILE`, `RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH`. `SSH_TPM_AUTH_SOCK` is also not unset. gpg finds its agent socket under `/run/user/<uid>/gnupg` by uid, so the private `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` does not hide the real gpg keyring and agent.

    - `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh:19-21` says "two pinned trees (node-runtime, orcad-template)". There are now three, with ripgrep.

# The app's fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here gets a
  # nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE instead of the distro's. Hermetic: nixpkgs'
  # own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set), whose 50-user.conf
  # pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font dirs, i.e. the
  # nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu, which the host
  # does not have:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by orca and macKeybindings; let bindings
  # are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # Mac-style shortcuts, the same Super-for-Cmd scheme as gtk's mac-bindings
  # and ghostty's super+c/v in home.nix: Orca's own macOS defaults, with Cmd
  # spelled out, which Orca binds to Super (event.metaKey) on Linux. The point
  # is that Ctrl and Meta stay the terminal's -- emacs keys reach the shell --
  # so no Ctrl- or Alt-only chord is left: not the Mac table's own
  # (Ctrl+1..9 tab select, Alt+Z word wrap, Ctrl+PageUp/Down), not a Linux
  # default. Only Ctrl+Tab stays, which the terminal receives as a bare Tab,
  # and the few orcaPinned below puts back on purpose.
  #
  # Generated from the app's own keybinding definitions at build time
  # (nix/orca-mac-keybindings.js), so a version bump picks up new actions.
  # Chords Hyprland binds would be dead keys, so those actions are unbound --
  # on shiori 19 of them, Super+F (find) and Super+P (go to file) among them,
  # plus Super+B/N/E, the digits, and their Shift forms. orcaPinned below
  # rebinds the ones worth having elsewhere. The build log lists every one.
  #
  # A running Orca reads the file once; after a switch, restart it (or run its
  # keybindings reload) for the new table to apply. Resetting a generated
  # shortcut in Orca's settings re-applies the Mac chord at the next switch:
  # Orca stores a reset, and a pick of its own Linux default, as the same
  # deletion, so neither sticks -- set some other chord, or unbind, instead.
  #
  # Find goes on Ctrl+S, emacs' isearch, everywhere but the terminal; there
  # C-s is the shell's own search, so terminal search is left unbound.
  #
  # Previous/next worktree, in list order, on Alt+Up/Down: the Mac chord,
  # Super+Shift+Up/Down, is Hyprland's. Orca catches it before any widget, so
  # this takes M-<up>/<down> from the terminal and the editor's move-line too,
  # deliberately.
  orcaPinned = {
    "editor.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
    "browser.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
    "chat.find" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
    "settings.search" = [ "Ctrl+S" ];
    "worktree.navigateUp" = [ "Alt+ArrowUp" ];
    "worktree.navigateDown" = [ "Alt+ArrowDown" ];
  };

content.text: The host's fontconfig is the same version as nixpkgs' (2.18.3), and it has 2652 fonts. Switching `fontsConf` to "the host's config plus DejaVu":

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='orca.nix'
s=open(p).read()
a=s.index("  # The app's fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here gets a")
b=s.index("  # Extracted once, shared by orca and macKeybindings")
s=s[:a]+'''  # The app's fontconfig: the host's own, plus DejaVu. Orca's Linux
  # terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with no
  # fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono
  # grid; the host does not have it. Scoped to orca rather than the profile
  # because only orca hardcodes it.
  #
  # The host's, not a hermetic nixpkgs conf.d: FONTCONFIG_FILE is inherited
  # by everything Orca spawns, which, unsandboxed, is the host's own programs,
  # and they must keep seeing the host's fonts (pacman's included) -- this
  # adds one family to what they see and takes nothing away. The host's
  # conf.d links into /usr/share/fontconfig resolve now; under bwrap they
  # dangled, which is why this used to be nixpkgs' conf.d. Its 50-user.conf
  # still pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig, home-manager's font dirs.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" \'\'
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">/etc/fonts/fonts.conf</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
    </fontconfig>
  \'\';
'''+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
grep -n "fontsConf = " -A7 orca.nix

# Once no bwrap-era Orca is left running anywhere, that path can go.
#
# That the two pinned trees (resources/node-runtime, resources/orcad-template)
# stay the AppImage's byte for byte is the derivation's installCheckPhase, not
# a case here: it gates the build.
#
# The GUI case (5) needs no desktop and never shows on one: it starts its own
# headless sway (wlroots' headless backend, a private XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) and
# runs Orca in that, with its own --user-data-dir and a throwaway HOME, so it
# never touches a running Orca's profile, ~/.orca/agent-hooks or
# ~/.claude/settings.json. ORCA_TEST_SHOT=<file.png> keeps its screenshot.
#
#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh               build this host's orca and test it
#   tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh <orca-path>   test a given build, e.g. the live one:
#                                               $(dirname $(dirname $(readlink -f ~/.nix-profile/bin/orca-ide)))
set -u
# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.
# grep -c reads it all: -q exits early, and under pipefail nix-store's
# SIGPIPE would send a hit to the else branch.
if [ "$(nix-store -qR "$ORCA" | grep -c -- '-bubblewrap-')" != 0 ]; then
  fail "no sandbox" "bubblewrap is in the closure of $ORCA"
else
  pass "no bubblewrap in the closure"
fi

  [ -n "$want" ] && [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "child sees host's '$c' ($want)" \
    || fail "$c" "child got '$got', host has '$want'"
done
# Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono", one
# family with no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another
# mono font; the host has no DejaVu, so orca.nix's fontsConf must apply.
got=$(node_run "fc-list -f '%{family[0]}\n' 'DejaVu Sans Mono' | sort -u | head -1")
[ "$got" = "DejaVu Sans Mono" ] && pass "'DejaVu Sans Mono' exists for the app (terminal default)" \
  || fail "DejaVu" "app's fontconfig has '${got:-nothing}'"
for c in 'sans\-serif:Noto Sans' 'monospace:Noto Sans Mono'; do
  pat=${c%%:*}; want=${c#*:}
  got=$(node_run "fc-match -f '%{family[0]}' '$pat'")
  [ "$got" = "$want" ] && pass "$pat -> $want for the app" \
    || fail "$pat" "resolves to '${got:-nothing}', want '$want'"
done

# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty, loaded by this Electron, opens a pty.
got=$(host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e '
  const p = require(process.argv[1]).spawn("/bin/sh", ["-c", "echo pty-ok"], {});
  let o = ""; p.onData(d => o += d);
  p.onExit(e => setTimeout(() => console.log(o.trim(), e.exitCode), 200));' \
  "$APP/resources/node_modules/node-pty" 2>&1)

{ config, lib, pkgs, machine, ... }:

let
  isDarwin = pkgs.stdenv.hostPlatform.isDarwin;
  isDesktop = machine.gui or true;

  # Orca (onorca.dev) — the agent IDE: parallel CLI agents, each in its own
  # worktree. Closed-source Electron app, not in nixpkgs (nixpkgs' `orca` is
  # the GNOME screen reader), so this packages the official Linux AppImage.
  # The electron-updater feed in each GitHub release, latest-linux.yml, is
  # the source of truth for version + sha512 when bumping: the yml's sha512
  # is the AppImage's, checked against
  # the download with `nix hash to-sri --type sha512 <sha512sum>`.
  # https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/latest/download/latest-linux.yml
  pname = "orca";
  version = "1.4.238";
  src = pkgs.fetchurl {
    url = "https://github.com/stablyai/orca/releases/download/v${version}/orca-linux.AppImage";
    hash = "REDACTED/sHSKlfJa4c1O2MCcdJhLrxCVm/NVKT+JtghzxoEsQ==";
  };

  # Wrap the AppImage (not autoPatchelf of the .deb) so the Electron stack
  # runs in appimageTools' FHS env, which works on non-NixOS hosts. Electron
  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.
  orca = pkgs.appimageTools.wrapType2 {
    inherit pname version src;
    extraPkgs = pkgs: [ pkgs.libsecret ];
    # The sandbox gets its own fontconfig, the way every other nix GUI app here
    # gets a nix-generated FONTCONFIG_FILE, instead of the distro's.
    # buildFHSEnv binds the host's /etc/fonts in, assuming NixOS; Arch's conf.d
    # links point into /usr/share/fontconfig, which the sandbox's /usr replaces,
    # so all of them dangled and every family fell to Montserrat Thin. See
    # fontsConf below. tests/sandbox-fonts.sh.
    extraBwrapArgs = [ "--setenv FONTCONFIG_FILE ${fontsConf}" ];
    # `orca-ide open` (orcaCli below) spawns the GUI detached, but every
    # wrapper layer execs the next, so this bwrap is the CLI's own child, and
    # --die-with-parent SIGKILLs the window the moment `open` returns. The
    # cost: bwrap forwards no signals, so when `orca-ide serve` is stopped by
    # a signal to the CLI (not Ctrl-C, which reaches the whole group, nor a
    # systemd cgroup stop), its Electron server outlives the bwrap it was
    #
    # The flag lands in extraInstallCommands, not postFixup: wrapType2 is a
    # buildFHSEnv, whose buildCommand short-circuits genericBuild's phase
    # list, so postFixup never runs. The bwrap launcher's bin/orca moves aside
    # to .orca-ide-unwrapped -- `orca` is orcaCli's name in the profile, and
    # tests/sandbox-fonts.sh finds the launcher by this one -- and
    # orca-ide-app execs it, the flag first when due.
    extraInstallCommands = ''
      mv $out/bin/orca $out/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped
      cat > $out/bin/orca-ide-app <<'EOF'
      #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
      explicit=
      for a in "$@"; do
        case $a in --) break ;; --ozone-platform|--ozone-platform=*) explicit=1; break ;; esac
      done
      if [ -z "$explicit" ] && [ -z "''${ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE:-}" ]; then
        set -- --ozone-platform=wayland "$@"
      fi
      exec ${placeholder "out"}/bin/.orca-ide-unwrapped "$@"
      EOF
      chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide-app
      install -Dm444 ${appimageContents}/orca-ide.desktop \
        $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop
      for size in 16 24 32 48 64 128 256 512; do
        install -Dm444 \
          ${appimageContents}/usr/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png \
          $out/share/icons/hicolor/''${size}x''${size}/apps/orca-ide.png
      done
      substituteInPlace $out/share/applications/orca-ide.desktop \
        --replace-fail 'Exec=AppRun' 'Exec=orca-ide-app'
    '';
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide-app";
  };
  # Hermetic: nixpkgs' own conf.d (store paths, the full standard alias set),
  # whose 50-user.conf pulls in ~/.config/fontconfig -- home-manager's font
  # dirs, i.e. the nix-profile fonts every other app here uses. Plus DejaVu:
  # Orca's Linux terminalFontFamily default is exactly "DejaVu Sans Mono" with
  # no fallback, and Chromium refuses fontconfig's alias to another mono font,
  # so without it the terminal lays a proportional fallback out on a mono grid.
  # Scoped to orca rather than the profile because only orca hardcodes it.
  fontsConf = pkgs.writeText "orca-fonts.conf" ''
    <?xml version="1.0"?>
    <!DOCTYPE fontconfig SYSTEM "urn:fontconfig:fonts.dtd">
    <fontconfig>
      <include ignore_missing="no">${pkgs.fontconfig.out}/etc/fonts/conf.d</include>
      <dir>${pkgs.dejavu_fonts}/share/fonts</dir>
      <cachedir prefix="xdg">fontconfig</cachedir>
    </fontconfig>
  '';
  # Extracted once, shared by the wrapper's extraInstallCommands below;
  # let bindings are recursive, so position in the block does not matter.
  appimageContents = pkgs.appimageTools.extract { inherit pname version src; };

  # nixGL wrap: without it the FHS env resolves GBM/DRI via the NixOS-only
  # /run/opengl-driver path and falls back to software rendering — the
  # same reason parsec gets it.
  orcaGui = config.lib.nixGL.wrap orca;

  # The CLI, as `orca-ide` (what the skills run outside an Orca terminal on
  # Linux) and `orca`. Upstream avoids bare `orca` on Linux because it is
  # usually the GNOME screen reader; it is not installed here, so `orca` is
  # the CLI too. (Were it installed, the profile comes first on PATH --
  # env.nix -- so `orca` would still be this CLI.) The skills say `orca-ide`.
  #
  # It is plain JavaScript: upstream's resources/bin/orca-ide runs it on the
  # bundled Electron in node mode, but nothing in it needs Electron, so it
  # runs on nixpkgs' node of the same major (Electron 43 bundles node 24)
  # with no sandbox -- a plain exec, so signals and exit codes are the CLI's
  # own. Orca's own installer puts a shim dir on PATH only in Orca
  # terminals, and a ~/.local/bin symlink to a raw store path that goes
  # stale on the next bump.
  #
  # ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE: the Orca binary for `orca-ide open` and `serve` to
  # launch; under plain node there is no other, and without it `open` fails
  # and `serve` refuses to start. NODE_OPTIONS is handed over as
  # ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS and cleared, as upstream's shim does.
  # tests/orca-cli-skills.sh.
  orcaCli = pkgs.runCommand "orca-cli-${version}" {
    pname = "orca-cli";
    inherit version;
    meta.mainProgram = "orca-ide";
  } ''
    mkdir -p $out/bin
    cat > $out/bin/orca-ide <<'EOF'
    #!${pkgs.runtimeShell}
    export ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE="''${ORCA_APP_EXECUTABLE:-${orcaGui}/bin/orca-ide-app}"
    export ORCA_NODE_OPTIONS="''${NODE_OPTIONS-}"
    export ORCA_NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE="''${NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE-}"
    unset NODE_OPTIONS NODE_REPL_EXTERNAL_MODULE
    exec ${pkgs.nodejs_24}/bin/node ${appimageContents}/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js "$@"
    EOF
    chmod +x $out/bin/orca-ide
    ln -s orca-ide $out/bin/orca
  '';

  # Orca's agent skills, from the repo at the commit this AppImage was built
  # from: `orca skills install` pins `npx skills add` to it, and the bundled
  # resources/skills/current-manifest.json holds their sha256s. Bump this rev
  # with the version — it is the `sourceCommit` in out/main/index.js of
  # app.asar, and the test holds it to that. A fetch in this module rather
  # than a flake input, because the rev tracks `version` above, not the
  # repo's head; `nix flake update` does not touch it. The rev is in the
  # store name so a rev bump without a hash bump fails to fetch instead of
  # reusing the old tree. The skills are stubs that call
  # `orca-ide skills get <name>`, so they need orcaCli above.
  #
  # A subset of the bundled ten: no Jira, no emulator. Each is a read-only
  # store symlink, so Orca's own Settings > Skills "update" (npx skills add)
  # will fail on them or replace them, and home-manager then refuses to
  # clobber; update by bumping here instead.
  orcaSkillsSrc = pkgs.fetchFromGitHub rec {
    name = "orca-skills-${rev}";
    owner = "stablyai";
    repo = "orca";
    rev = "e6f7fba58e8e47b45e4343f99101b3ca9e05a5da";
    hash = "REDACTED";

orca serve

Usage: orca serve [--port <port>] [--pairing-address <host>] [--mobile-pairing] [--no-pairing] [--grant-desktop-control] [--project-root <path>] [--recipe-json] [--supervise] [--force] [--json]

Start an Orca runtime server without opening a desktop window

Options:
  --help                 Show this help message
  --json                 Emit machine-readable JSON
  --pairing-code <code>  Run against a remote Orca server using an orca://pair?... code
  --environment <selector> Run against a saved paired Orca server (id or name); terminal handles belong to the server that issued them
  --port
  --pairing-address
  --mobile-pairing
  --no-pairing
  --grant-desktop-control
  --project-root
  --recipe-json
  --supervise
  --force                Force worktree removal when supported; does not force branch deletion
  --page <id>            Stable browser page id from `orca tab list --json`

Notes:
  Runs in the foreground and prints the bound endpoint, advertised endpoint, and pairing status. Stop it with Ctrl+C.
  With --port, serve exits with an error when that port is already in use. Without it, serve uses 6768 and moves to another port when 6768 is taken.
  --pairing-address changes only the client-advertised address; use a reachable LAN, Tailscale, SSH-forward, or reverse-proxy endpoint.
  Use --recipe-json with --project-root from VM recipes to print the recipe result JSON and leave the server running.
  Use --mobile-pairing to print a mobile-scoped pairing QR/link instead of the default runtime-environment pairing link.
  A paired client cannot drive this machine's desktop (orca computer) unless the offer was created with --grant-desktop-control.
  When the web client bundle is available, the server also prints a browser URL with the pairing data embedded.
  Exits with code 3, without starting anything, when another Orca already serves this profile or cannot be shown to have stopped.
  On macOS, after Orca serve aborts at startup (it could not register with Launch Services), later runs from the same environment refuse for 30 minutes with exit code 78. Use --force to try anyway.
  --supervise is for service managers (launchd, systemd). Orca serve then restarts the server itself with growing delays instead of exiting when it stops, waits while an update replaces the app, and waits while another Orca serves this profile. After 6 failures in 15 minutes it gives up and exits with code 0 so the manager stops too, and later supervised runs refuse until a new build is installed or --force is passed. Not available on Windows yet.
  Experimental and off by default: set ORCA_TERMINAL_PROCESS_CEILING=<n> (64 or more) before the terminal host starts to have the OS cap how many processes each terminal may run (Linux, through a systemd user scope per terminal, which needs a user manager that outlives logout; Windows, through a job per terminal). `orca serve` reports the ceiling as on or off, with the reason.
  Off by default: set ORCA_TERMINAL_MEMORY_MAX=<size> (256M or more) and ORCA_TERMINAL_MEMORY_SWAP_MAX=<size> (0 for no swap) before the terminal host starts to cap the memory and swap of each terminal on Linux, through the same per-terminal systemd user scope. A terminal over its limit has its largest process OOM-killed; the host and other terminals keep running. Sizes take K, M, G or T. A limit the host cannot enforce is skipped and logged in the terminal host log. No effect on macOS or Windows.

Examples:
  $ orca serve
  $ orca serve --json
  $ orca serve --project-root /workspace/repo --pairing-address wss://sandbox.example.com --recipe-json

  # safeStorage wants libsecret at runtime.

content.content:
# The GUI wrapper's argv decision, on the real generated script with its
# final exec swapped for a printf, so nothing launches: --ozone-platform=
# wayland first, except in node mode or when the caller names a platform
# itself -- `--ozone-platform` or `--ozone-platform=...` before any `--`,
# the rule of Orca's own hasExplicitOzonePlatform; a -hint does not count.
inner=$(grep -o '/nix/store/[^ ]*/bin/orca-ide-app' "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" | tail -1)
[ -n "$inner" ] || inner="$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app"  # no nixGL layer
sed -E 's|^exec .*/\.orca-ide-unwrapped "\$@"$|printf "%s\\n" "$@"|' "$inner" > "$T/argv"
grep -q '^printf' "$T/argv" && ! grep -q 'orca-ide-unwrapped' "$T/argv" \
  || { echo "could not swap the one exec line in $inner" >&2; exit 1; }
argv() { env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE bash "$T/argv" "$@" | paste -sd' '; }
for c in "open|--ozone-platform=wayland open" \
         "--serve --ozone-platform=x11|--serve --ozone-platform=x11" \
         "--ozone-platform x11|--ozone-platform x11" \
         "--ozone-platform=|--ozone-platform=" \
         "--ozone-platform-hint=auto|--ozone-platform=wayland --ozone-platform-hint=auto" \
else fail "orca-ide-app node mode" "$(cat "$T/node-out")$(tail -1 "$T/node-err")"; fi

# `orca-ide open` spawns the GUI detached, waits for it (up to 15s), then
# exits. Each GUI wrapper layer execs the next, so the GUI's bwrap is the
# CLI's own child; with --die-with-parent it would be SIGKILLed the moment
# `open` returns. The parent here stays up past bwrap's startup, as `open`
# does: one that exits first never arms bwrap's parent-death signal at all.
if [ -z "$node_ok" ]; then
  fail "GUI lifetime" "skipped: node mode failed above, so this would launch a real GUI"
else
ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 nodisplay bash -c '"$1" -e "
  setTimeout(() => require(\"fs\").writeFileSync(process.argv[1], \"alive\"), 6000);
  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 7000);" "$2" >/dev/null 2>&1 & sleep 4' _ "$GUI/bin/orca-ide-app" "$T/alive"
for _ in $(seq 75); do [ -s "$T/alive" ] && break; sleep 0.2; done
if [ -s "$T/alive" ]; then pass "the GUI outlives the parent that spawned it (orca-ide open)"
else fail "GUI lifetime" "no alive marker within 15s (died with its parent, or never started)"; fi
fi

content.text:
Both points from the CLI session are handled, and review round 4 is running on the merged HEAD (f2f78a6f). The `orca-cli-node` branch still isn't on master, so I merged it into this branch rather than wait.

**1. Signal to `orca-ide serve`:** case 6 in `tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh`.
- It starts `serve` forced onto the Electron runtime, in an isolated session (Xvfb, its own D-Bus, throwaway HOME), sends SIGTERM to the CLI, and fails if any Electron process survives.
- Against the CLI branch's sandboxed GUI it fails: all 8 Electron processes were left running. Against this build it passes: all 7 went down with the CLI.
- By default `serve` runs on orcad, which is the pinned, unpatched node. Killing the CLI takes that down too, and it shows the pinned trees run unsandboxed.

**2. Rename and the CLI branch's tests:**
- The GUI is now `orca-ide-app`, and the build fails unless the desktop Exec is exactly `orca-ide-app %U`.
- The CLI branch's rule moved into my wrapper: no wayland flag when the caller passes `--ozone-platform` (as `serve` does with x11).
- `dieWithParent` is gone along with the sandbox.
- In `tests/orca-cli-skills.sh`, the GUI argv check and the GUI-lifetime check (window outliving `orca-ide open`) are updated for the new wrapper.

On the merged tree: GUI tests 23/23, CLI tests 25/25, keybinding tests 32/32.

Round 3 also changed the fonts: Orca and everything it spawns now see your host's font config plus DejaVu. The old private config hid 627 of the host's font files from Orca's terminals.

**Still open:**
- Two clean review rounds in a row on this HEAD.
- If the CLI branch reaches master as different commits (rebased or squashed), I'll re-merge and review again.
- Your answer on nixGL: keep, drop, or strip the variables it passes into Orca's terminals.
- Then merge to master and run `hms`.

# that Noto Color Emoji had, plus control pictures and arrows the text fonts
  # had, and fontconfig ranks it first for many of them -- for a sans request
  # on fontconfig 2.18 by genericfamily, which no family-order rule in conf.d
  # outranks. So it is cut down at build time (nix/font-gaps.py) to only the
  # codepoints none of yieldTo has: it can only be reached for a glyph that
  # would otherwise be tofu. yieldTo must be exactly the other font packages in
  # the profile; tests/symbol-fonts.sh checks both directions -- every font it
  # needs to yield to is in yieldTo (by font files on hosts of the running
  # machine's system, by name on all), and everything in yieldTo is installed
  # -- plus the fallback for a mono and a sans request.
  # It covers the profile only: orca's sandbox DejaVu stays out on purpose --
  # yielding to it would cut ~480 glyphs that are tofu outside orca, and
  # inside it fontconfig already ranks DejaVu ahead (measured: nothing moves).
  #
  # The source face comes from the cached noto-fonts, not
  # `noto-fonts.override { variants = ...; }`, whose build needs the whole
  # monthly release (cache.nixos.org has only the default build: a 27 MB
  # download). The script fails the build if upstream moves the file.
  symbolsGapFont = let
    yieldTo = [
      googleFonts pkgs.nerd-fonts.jetbrains-mono pkgs.noto-fonts-color-emoji
====
#     installed -- a font it yields to but nothing installs is a hole, tofu
#     again (hosts are read out of the flake).
#     Every host is checked by package name, an eval only; on hosts of this
#     machine's system, also by font files: any package already in the local
#     store with a font under share/fonts must be yielded to, whatever its
#     name (jetbrains-mono, inter, iosevka never say "font");
#   * on hosts of this machine's system, the realised face still covers the
#     glyphs below, checked with fc-query;
#   * on those hosts, fallback through a throwaway fontconfig over nixpkgs'
#     conf.d (what orca.nix includes) with the gap font and what it yields
#     to: ⏵ and 🬀
#     reach the gap font, ⏸🖥⭐ still reach Noto Color Emoji and ␀ a text font
#     -- for a monospace request and for a sans one.
#
#   ./tests/symbol-fonts.sh            # tests this checkout
#   ./tests/symbol-fonts.sh /path/to/flake
set -u
set -o pipefail

FLAKE="${1:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)}"
[ -f "$FLAKE/flake.nix" ] || { echo "no flake.nix in: $FLAKE" >&2; exit 1; }
...
  # to, nothing from the host, over nixpkgs' conf.d.
  # Realised by drv, but only the default outputs are used: google-fonts also
  # has an adobeBlank output -- blank glyphs for every codepoint -- which the
  # profile never links and which would otherwise win every fallback.
  # shellcheck disable=SC2046
  nix-store --realise $(jq -r '.yieldTo[]' <<<"$info") >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || { fail "$h: fallback" "could not realise the fonts it yields to"; continue; }
  dirs=$(jq -r '.yieldToOut[]' <<<"$info")
  fc=$(nix build --no-link --print-out-paths "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$h.pkgs.fontconfig.out" 2>/dev/null) \
    || { fail "$h: fallback" "could not realise fontconfig"; continue; }

content.text: Adding one `appnode` helper for every node-mode call. It strips the display variables and points `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` at an empty directory, so even a lost node mode can't reach any compositor:

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
import re
p='tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(o,n,cnt=1):
    global s
    assert s.count(o)==cnt, (s.count(o),o[:60]); s=s.replace(o,n)
rep('''# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.''','''# Every node-mode run of the GUI, with no way to a display: were node mode
# ever lost, this would be a GUI launch, and it must fail rather than open a
# window on the live desktop -- no WAYLAND_DISPLAY/DISPLAY, and a runtime dir
# with no socket in it (unset, Wayland falls back to wayland-0 there).
mkdir -p -m700 "$T/nodisplay"
appnode() { host timeout 120 env -u WAYLAND_DISPLAY -u WAYLAND_SOCKET -u DISPLAY \\
  XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$T/nodisplay" ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" "$@"; }

# 1. No bwrap anywhere in the launch chain.''')
rep('''got=$(host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -p 1 2>&1)''','''got=$(appnode -p 1 2>&1)''')
rep('''  host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \\''','''  appnode -e \\''')
rep('''got=$(host timeout 120 env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \'''','''got=$(appnode -e \'''')
rep('''  pid=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \'''','''  pid=$(appnode -e \'''')
rep('''  colours=$(host env ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "$GUI" -e \'''','''  colours=$(appnode -e \'''')
# case 6 CLI resolution
a=s.index('cli=${ORCA_CLI:-}'); b=s.index('cat > "$T/serve.sh" <<EOF')
s=s[:a]+'''cli=${ORCA_CLI:-}
if [ -z "$cli" ]; then
  # Realised by drv, as the GUI is above: a bare output path cannot be built.
  clidrv=$(nix eval --raw "$FLAKE#homeConfigurations.$HOSTNAME_.config.home.packages" \\
    --apply 'ps: let c = builtins.filter (p: builtins.match "orca-cli-[0-9.]+" (p.name or "") != null) ps;
                 in if c == [] then "" else (builtins.head c).drvPath') \\
    || { echo "could not evaluate home.packages for orca-cli" >&2; exit 1; }
  if [ -n "$clidrv" ]; then
    cli=$(nix-store --realise "$clidrv" | tail -1)/bin/orca-ide
    [ -x "$cli" ] || { echo "could not build the profile's orca-cli ($clidrv)" >&2; exit 1; }
  else
    cli="$node24/bin/node $APP/resources/app.asar.unpacked/out/cli/index.js"
  fi
fi
echo "serve via: $cli"
'''+s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
grep -n 'ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE=1 "\$GUI"' tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh; bash -n tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh && echo ok

content.thinking: I'm verifying that every glyph DejaVu shares with the gap font stays assigned to DejaVu for mono and sans requests, then I'll address the two missing dlopen checks for libEGL.so and libvk_swiftshader.so.

input.command:
python3 - <<'PYEOF'
p='tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh'; s=open(p).read()
def rep(o,n):
    global s
    assert o in s, o[:60]; s=s.replace(o,n)
rep('''# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty''','''# home.nix's symbol gap font does not yield to DejaVu (that would cut glyphs
# that are tofu outside Orca); it relies on fontconfig ranking DejaVu ahead
# wherever both have a glyph, under the app's own fontconfig. Every such
# glyph, for a mono and a sans request.
gapcheck='
gap=$(fc-list -f "%{file}\\n" "Noto Sans Symbols 2" | grep -m1 Gaps) || { echo nogap; exit; }
cps() { fc-query -f "%{charset}\\n" "$1" | tr " " "\\n" | awk -F- "NF { a = strtonum(\\"0x\\" \\$1); b = \\$2 == \\"\\" ? a : strtonum(\\"0x\\" \\$2); for (i = a; i <= b; i++) printf \\"%x\\\\n\\", i }" | sort -u; }
cps "$gap" > "$0.gap"
for pair in "monospace:DejaVu Sans Mono" "sans\\-serif:DejaVu Sans"; do
  req=${pair%%:*}; fam=${pair#*:}
  cps "$(fc-list -f "%{file}\\n" "$fam:style=Book" | head -1)" | comm -12 - "$0.gap" > "$0.both"
  moved=0; while read -r cp; do
    [ "$(fc-match -f "%{family[0]}" "$req:charset=$cp")" = "Noto Sans Symbols 2" ] && moved=$((moved+1))
  done < "$0.both"
  echo "$fam $moved $(wc -l < "$0.both")"
done'
got=$(node_run "$(printf '%s' "$gapcheck" | sed "s|\\$0|$T/gapcheck|g")")
case $got in
  nogap) echo "skip gap-font ranking: no Noto Sans Symbols 2 gap font on this host" ;;
  *) while read -r f1 f2 f3 moved total; do
       fam="$f1 $f2 $f3"; [ "$f3" = "$moved" ] && { fam="$f1 $f2"; total=$moved; moved=$f3; }
       [ "${total:-0}" -gt 0 ] && [ "$moved" = 0 ] \\
         && pass "$fam keeps all $total glyphs it shares with the symbol gap font" \\
         || fail "gap font" "$fam: $moved of ${total:-?} shared glyphs go to the gap font"
     done <<< "$got" ;;
esac

# Orca's terminals: the patched node-pty''')
rep('''       dlopens "$APP/libGLESv2.so" libEGL.so.1 libGL.so.1''','''       for gl in libGLESv2.so libEGL.so libvk_swiftshader.so; do dlopens "$APP/$gl" libEGL.so.1 libGL.so.1; done''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
PYEOF
bash -n tests/orca-gui-unsandboxed.sh && echo ok

Review round 4's findings are all fixed, and round 5 is running on the new HEAD (0af5df11). No round has come back clean yet, so the two-in-a-row count is still at zero.

What changed in round 4:
- **Test can no longer touch your desktop:** every node-mode run of the GUI now has no display variables and an empty runtime dir. If node mode ever broke, the run would fail instead of opening a window.
- **The `serve` test uses the real CLI:** it now runs through the profile's `orca-cli` and prints which one ran. Before, it could silently fall back to running the CLI script directly.
- **Symbol gap font checked under Orca's font config:** DejaVu keeps all 143 (Mono) and 476 (Sans) glyphs it shares with `home.nix`'s gap font, so nothing changes face inside Orca. Comments carried over in the merge that still described the old sandboxed font setup are fixed.
- **Stray file removed:** a reviewer wrote `/dev/shm/x` (a codepoint list) against instructions. I checked it and deleted it.

The test suite passes 25/25.

Still waiting on you: keep, drop, or strip the nixGL variables that reach Orca's terminals.

Master hasn't moved, so the CLI branch is still merged in here directly rather than through master.
